biology.nervous-prac-plan.0002.all: Plan: vary light intensity (lamp distance / light meter, 5 values); measure pupil diameter with ruler/photo with scale; wait set time to adjust; same person, same eye, same distance; repeat + mean; safety: no direct bright light

biology.nervous-prac-reliab.0002.a: calculate a mean; identify anomalies; more reliable as pupil size varies
biology.nervous-prac-reliab.0002.b: measure pupil in normal room light with no change / keep other eye conditions same; shows change is due to light intensity

biology.nervous-prac-risk.0001.a: ruler could hit/poke eye or fingers - keep face away, drop from set height; spilled drink/allergies - check
biology.nervous-prac-risk.0001.b: repeat and take mean / read the ruler at eye level at the top of the thumb / use same starting point at 0 cm

biology.nervous-prac-step.0003.all: pupil reflex takes time to respond/adjust; so pupil has reached its final (steady) diameter before measurement

biology.nervous-prac-vars.0001.b: distance ruler falls before caught (reaction time)
biology.nervous-prac-vars.0001.c: same hand; same starting height/position of ruler; same person dropping; same volume of cola; time after drinking

biology.nervous-recall-multi.0002.a: stimulus - receptor - sensory neurone - relay neurone - motor neurone - effector - response

biology.plant-nutrition-data-graph.0002.a: rate increases as light intensity increases, rapidly at first then slows and levels off (~37 bubbles/min from ~50 au); quote data
biology.plant-nutrition-data-graph.0002.b: at low intensity light is limiting factor so rate rises with light; at high intensity another factor (CO2 conc or temperature) limits so plateau

biology.plant-nutrition-data-pct.0004.b: above 30 C (optimum) enzymes controlling photosynthesis denature; active site shape changes; rate falls

biology.plant-nutrition-data-plot.0001.a: light intensity x, rate y, points plotted, smooth curve
biology.plant-nutrition-data-plot.0001.b: rate increases with light intensity, increase slows, levels off at 37 bubbles per minute from 50 au

biology.plant-nutrition-data-read.0004.b: (25-10)/(35-10) = 0.6 au per C (if graph matches table)
biology.plant-nutrition-data-read.0004.c: above optimum 30 C enzymes denature, active site changes shape, rate falls

biology.plant-nutrition-describe.0005.all: pondweed in water under funnel with inverted test tube of water; place in light; collect gas; test with glowing splint which relights = oxygen

biology.plant-nutrition-describe-multi.0.b: CO2 diffuses in through stomata; through air spaces in spongy mesophyll to cells; O2 diffuses out through stomata, down concentration gradients

biology.plant-nutrition-explain.0002.all: large surface area to absorb more light and for gas exchange; thin so short diffusion distance for CO2 to reach cells / light reaches all cells

biology.plant-nutrition-explain-multi.00.b: remove existing starch so any starch found later must have been made during the experiment; otherwise false positive

biology.plant-nutrition-ext.0010.all: Plan: photosynthesis enzyme-controlled; rising temp increases KE, collisions, ES complexes, rate up to optimum; above optimum enzymes denature, active site changes, rate falls rapidly; low temp limiting factor; link to graph shape

biology.plant-nutrition-mcq-rev.0005.all: Brings water to the leaf for photosynthesis

biology.plant-nutrition-prac-method.0002.all: destarch plant in dark 48 h; place in light for some hours; draw/record green and white areas; boil leaf in water, then hot ethanol to remove chlorophyll, rinse; add iodine; green areas blue-black, white areas orange-brown

biology.plant-nutrition-prac-plan.0001.all: Plan: pondweed in water with NaHCO3; vary lamp distance (5 values) or light meter; count bubbles / collect O2 in set time; acclimatise; control temp (heat shield/water bath), CO2 conc, same plant; repeat + mean

biology.plant-nutrition-prac-reliab.0002.a: calculate a mean, identify anomalies, more reliable
biology.plant-nutrition-prac-reliab.0002.b: test a leaf from a destarched plant kept in the dark (or all-green leaf) - shows starch is due to photosynthesis in light / green areas

biology.plant-nutrition-prac-risk.0003.a: lamp gets hot - do not touch/allow to cool; water near electrics - keep apart
biology.plant-nutrition-prac-risk.0003.b: collect gas in gas syringe or capillary tube (photosynthometer) instead of counting bubbles

biology.plant-nutrition-prac-step.0001.all: water absorbs heat from lamp; keeps temperature constant so only light intensity affects the rate

biology.plant-nutrition-ext.0010.problem: Indicative content is a generic limiting-factor template (more energy/raw material, graph levels off) that does not fit temperature; omits kinetic energy/collisions and optimum, and temperature does not cause levelling off.
biology.plant-nutrition-ext.0010.fix: Points: photosynthesis is enzyme-controlled; rising temperature increases kinetic energy and enzyme-substrate collisions so rate rises; temperature limiting at low values; optimum temperature (~25-35 C); above optimum enzymes denature, active site changes shape, rate falls rapidly; at high temperature stomata may close reducing CO2 uptake.

biology.plant-nutrition-prac-reliab.0002.fix: MS: the white (non-green) areas of the same leaf act as the control (1); shows starch is only made where chlorophyll is present / any difference is due to chlorophyll (1).
